description: WFCAM is the wide-field near-infrared camera on UKIRT and the camera used for UKIDSS. These bands are the Z, Y, J, H and K passbands of the WFCAM photometric system published by Hewett et al.
facility_description: The United Kingdom Infrared Telescope (UKIRT) is a 3.8 m infrared telescope on Mauna Kea, and WFCAM is its wide-field camera.
notes: Hewett et al. 2006 give the default ZYJHK curves as system throughput from above the atmosphere to the detector (1.3 airmass, 1.0 mm water), normalised to the measured photon count rate. The UKIDSS technical page offers those tables if you wish to produce your own synthetic colours and states no redistribution terms. The arXiv record uses the assumed 1991-2003 licence, which the arXiv reuse page treats as the non-exclusive licence; the stored sentence is from that page and requires contacting the author before further reuse. The numeric curves are therefore not clearly redistributable. J, H and K were made to the Mauna Kea specification; Z and Y are WFCAM bands, so PhotSystem is the paper's name for the set, ZYJHK, not MKO. The WSA citation text still contains the placeholders Xnd and XX et al (200X) and does not ask for a proposal id. Irwin et al. is given there once as 2008 and elsewhere as in preparation, with no bibcode. Casali et al. 2007 is cited by DOI because bibcode:2007A&A...467..777C failed check_refs. about.ifa.hawaii.edu timed out. The UKIDSS HTML citation is split by links, so the acknowledgement is the contiguous wording on the WSA publications page.

acknowledgements.text:
The UKIDSS project is defined in Lawrence et al 2007. UKIDSS uses the UKIRT
Wide Field Camera (WFCAM; Casali et al 2007) and a photometric system
described in Hewett et al 2006. The pipeline processing and science archive
are described in Irwin et al (2008) and Hambly et al (2008). We have used
data from the Xnd data release, which is described in detail in XX et al
(200X).
